2026-11-08.title: Second Sunday of the Dedication of the Church
2026-11-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (Syro-Malabar Liturgical Calendar)
readings: I will bring you into the promised land
My reward is with the Lord
An inheritance kept in heaven for you
You will sit on twelve thrones
2026-11-08.alt: Season of the Dedication of the Church (Qudash Edtha).
2026-11-08.verse: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or children or fields, for my name's sake, will receive a hundredfold, and will inherit eternal life.
theo: Today's readings speak of inheritance. In Egypt, crushed by slavery, Israel hears God's promise: “I will take you as my people, and I will be your God… I will bring you into the land… I will give it to you for a possession.” The promised land was never only a territory; it was life with God.

The Servant in Isaiah feels he has laboured in vain, “yet surely my cause is with the LORD, and my reward with my God.” Peter writes to scattered Christians that they have been born anew “into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you.” The Church is the people already on the way to that inheritance.

In the Gospel the disciples are shocked: if the rich can hardly enter the Kingdom, who can be saved? Jesus answers, “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.” Then Peter asks what they will receive for leaving everything. Jesus promises thrones, a hundredfold, and eternal life. The apostles, on whom the Church is founded, will share in Christ's judgement and glory.

For Kerala Christians, whose families have often been measured by land and property, this Gospel is searching. Our deepest inheritance is not the family property but the faith received from the apostle Thomas and handed down for centuries. What we leave for Christ is never lost; it returns a hundredfold.
conn: Exodus 6:6–8 has a chain of divine promises: I will free, deliver, redeem, take you as my people. Jewish tradition links them to the four cups of the Passover meal; at the Last Supper Jesus took one of those cups and made it the cup of the new covenant.
Isaiah 49:6 calls the Servant “a light to the nations”. Simeon applies this to the child Jesus in the Temple (Luke 2:32), and Paul to the Church's mission (Acts 13:47).
The twelve apostles correspond to the twelve tribes: the Church is the renewed Israel. Revelation 21:14 places the apostles' names on the twelve foundations of the heavenly Jerusalem.
Some later explanations speak of a small gate called the “needle's eye”, but there is no ancient evidence for it. Jesus deliberately uses an impossible image: salvation is God's work.
altar: Peter calls our inheritance “kept in heaven”. At the Qurbana we receive its pledge already: the Body and Blood of the risen Christ, “the medicine of immortality”, as St Ignatius of Antioch called it. Every Communion is a down payment on the inheritance.
outline: Ask: what will you leave behind for your children? Land, house, money, or faith?
Point 1 · God's promise of an inheritance
From Egypt to the promised land: God frees his people to belong to him.
Point 2 · An inheritance that does not fade
Peter: a living hope and a heavenly inheritance, tested like gold in fire.
Point 3 · Impossible for us, possible for God
Wealth cannot save; God's grace can. What we leave for Christ returns a hundredfold.
An old Kerala family Bible handed down for generations: the true family property.
live: Talk with your children this week about how faith came to your family.
Give something valuable to someone in need, freely.
Bring one “impossible” situation to God each day.
fathers: In “Who is the rich man that shall be saved?” he teaches that wealth itself is not condemned, but the soul's attachment to it; riches must be used for others.
He calls the Eucharist “the medicine of immortality, the antidote against death” (Letter to the Ephesians 20).
magis: Detachment from riches is necessary to enter the Kingdom.
Hope: we desire eternal life as our happiness, trusting in Christ's promises.
saints: 11 Nov: St Martin of Tours (Latin calendar). 12 Nov: St Josaphat, martyr for unity (Latin calendar).
2026-11-08.prayer: Father of mercy, you have given us new birth into a living hope and an inheritance kept in heaven. Free us from all that holds us back from following your Son, and make us faithful to the faith we have received, for all things are possible with you. Amen.

quick: Our true inheritance is life with God, kept in heaven.
Wealth cannot save us; for God all things are possible.
What we leave for Christ returns a hundredfold.
2026-11-08.action: Talk with your children about how faith came to your family.
2026-11-08.question: What am I holding on to that keeps me from following Christ?
2026-11-08.special: Second Sunday of Qudash Edtha. The readings speak of the inheritance God gives his people.
illus: Many Kerala families keep an old palm-leaf or printed family Bible with the names and baptism dates of their ancestors. Property gets divided and sold; that book is passed on whole. It is the real family inheritance.

family.explain: Jesus said that whoever gives up something for him will receive a hundred times more. The best thing our family has is our faith, and we want to pass it on.
family.intention: We pray for our ancestors who handed on the faith to us.

kidsaint: A bishop in Ukraine who worked all his life for the unity of Christians with the Pope. He gave his life for it. Lesson: unity in the Church is worth more than anything we own.
term: In the Bible, the land God promised to Israel; in the New Testament, eternal life with God, “imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven” (1 Peter 1:4).

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in Kerala we know a lot about inheritance: land, houses, gold, and sometimes long family disputes over them. Today God speaks to us about a different inheritance.

In Egypt the Israelites were slaves. God said to Moses: “I will take you as my people, and I will be your God. I will bring you into the land I promised.” The land was a gift, but the greater gift was God himself: “I will be your God.”

St Peter writes to Christians who had lost homes and property: God has given you new birth “into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you.” No one can steal it, divide it, or take it to court.

In the Gospel Jesus says it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the Kingdom. The disciples are shocked. Jesus says, “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.” And to those who leave everything for him he promises a hundredfold and eternal life.

So let us ask ourselves today: what am I leaving to my children? If we leave them land without faith, we leave them poor. If we leave them faith, we leave them an inheritance that will never fade. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what an inheritance is? It's something precious your parents and grandparents give you.
Jesus said the most precious gift is not money or land, but God himself and heaven, which no one can take away.
Let's thank God for our faith, the best gift from our families. Say together: “Jesus, you are my treasure!”

intro: Theme: “The inheritance that does not fade.”
From the promised land to the heavenly inheritance: God gives himself to his people, and what we leave for Christ returns a hundredfold.

sub: In Egypt God promises freedom, a people and a land.
The greatest gift is God himself: “I will be your God.”
The Church is the people on the way to the inheritance.
q: I will take you as my people, and I will be your God. You shall know that I am the LORD your God, who has freed you from the burdens of the Egyptians.
And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or children or fields, for my name's sake, will receive a hundredfold, and will inherit eternal life.
points.apply: Thank God for the freedom he has given you in Christ.

sub: The Servant's reward is with God, even when his labour seems vain.
Peter: an inheritance imperishable, undefiled, unfading.
Faith, not property, is the family's true wealth.
q: The LORD is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot. The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; I have a goodly heritage.

By his great mercy he has given us a new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, and into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you.
points.apply: Tell your children how faith came to your family.

points.h: Impossible for us, possible for God
sub: Riches cannot open the door of the Kingdom.
Salvation is God's work; we receive it with open hands.
The apostles who left everything will share Christ's glory.
q: But I said, “I have labored in vain, I have spent my strength for nothing and vanity; yet surely my cause is with the LORD, and my reward with my God.”
But Jesus looked at them and said, “For mortals it is impossible, but for God all things are possible.”
points.apply: Give something valuable to someone in need this week.

concl: What we keep we lose; what we give to Christ we keep forever.
Let us leave our children the inheritance of faith.
2026-11-08.resolve: Read 1 Peter 1:3–9 as a family this week.
